data.executive_summary:
Imagur (also operating as "FShare") runs an image-sharing web application at imagesharer.xyz (branded "Imager"), hosted on an OVH VPS with back-end storage and a database in AWS (Sydney region). A security assessment was performed from 05 to 06 October 2026, covering the web application, its origin infrastructure, and the associated AWS account.

The most severe issue is that the **AWS root account credentials are embedded in a publicly downloadable JavaScript file** (/js/awsvalid.js). Anyone who fetches this file obtains full administrative control of the organization's entire AWS account, including the storage bucket holding all customer image uploads and the application database.

A second serious issue is that the **S3 bucket (filesharer-research) storing every user's images is publicly listable and world-readable**. Images that users mark as "Private" are therefore still downloadable by anyone, and every user's internal identifier can be enumerated.

The web application also has a **stored cross-site scripting** vulnerability (via the uploaded filename) and **no cross-site request forgery protection**.

**Highest-priority actions:** (1) rotate and remove the exposed AWS root key; (2) lock down the S3 bucket so it is not publicly readable or listable; (3) fix the stored XSS and add CSRF protection.

A total of **11 findings** were confirmed: 1 critical, 2 high, 3 medium, 2 low, and 3 informational.

data.scope:
## In scope
* Web application: https://imagesharer.xyz/ and https://www.imagesharer.xyz/
* Origin infrastructure: 51.161.131.44 (OVH Sydney; nginx + PHP 8.2.34)
* CDN: resources.imagesharer.xyz -> CloudFront d273uevi0662l0.cloudfront.net
* AWS account 016170038077 (ap-southeast-2): S3 bucket filesharer-research, S3 bucket filesharer-research-testing (stale), RDS Aurora PostgreSQL database-2, CloudFront distribution EMOI8CZBQIEBR, IAM users console-admin and fokirohu, EC2 security group sg-0fb1d9ee18578a337, default VPC vpc-06f86289a752c416d.

## Out of scope
Third-party hosting/CDN providers (OVH ASN/netblocks, CloudFront edge IPs, Spaceship nameservers) and unrelated lookalike domains.

## Methodology
Non-intrusive enumeration (DNS, WHOIS, RDAP, TLS, passive subdomain/CT, read-only AWS API) followed by manual, non-destructive web application testing (authentication, authorization, IDOR, SQL injection, stored XSS, file-upload validation, S3 access control). Minimal proof-of-concept only; no destructive actions, no DoS, no brute force, no data exfiltration.
data.provided_users: None provided (black-box assessment performed unauthenticated and with self-registered test accounts).
